newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Cocoa prices hammered by speculative sales. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Cocoa prices hammered by speculative sales. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]

text.p: World cocoa prices slumped by as much as 10 percent on Thursday as a sharp reversal to the recent rally that took them to one-year highs was extended.
Cocoa had already shed almost nine percent this week before the day's heavy losses as investors continued their heavy selling.

At one point during the session September LIFFE cocoa futures plunged as much as 109 sterling to hit a low of 1,000 sterling per tonne before rebounding up to 1,020 sterling (corrects currency from dollars).

Until this week aggressive fund-led and industry buying had fuelled a run-up since mid-June amid a strong technical outlook and longer-term concerns about the impact of an El Nino weather pattern on future harvests.

Elsewhere on the commodity front, gold managed to nudge above Wednesday's fresh 4-1/4 lows of $331.45 per ounce despite heated selling on rumours, since confirmed, that the Reserve Bank of Australia had sold a chunk of its reserves.

The Australians confirmed they had sold 167 tonnes of gold to reduce the central bank's holdings to 80 tonnes. Last year the country was the world's third largest gold producer after South Africa and the United States, producing 289 tonnes.

Gold prices have been under pressure for a year but has intensified recently on rumours of central bank sales and forward selling from producers. The gloomy mood has provoked speculative funds into taking positions assuming the price would fall further and scaring potential buyers into stocks and bonds.
Bullion finished the day slightly lower at $331.75 an ounce versus $332.45 on Wednesday.

In base metals, zinc hit another fresh 6-3/4 year high at $1,495 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange -- bringing its two-week gains to almost 10 percent before the price slipped back to finish the day at $1,475 per tonne.
Profit-taking took some of the shine off the advance but underlying speculative interest remains strong and warehouse stocks remain tightly controlled.
Oil prices faced a bruising day as the market digested news that Iraq had completed an aid distribution plan under its United Nations' food-for-oil deal.
Iraq's U.N. coordinator announced that Baghdad and the United Nations had completed aid distribution plans to cover the next six months of oil exports and would send them for U.N. approval soon.
Finalisation of the plan is the next step towards the long-delayed resumption of oil sales.
Benchmark London Brent for August delivery finished the day down 46 cents at $18.46 per barrel.
